## 1. NVDA — NVIDIA Corporation ⭐ TOP PICK

**Price: $205.19 | Panel: 6 bulls / 4 neutral / 4 bears | Signal: BUY**

### The Business
NVIDIA designs the world's leading GPUs — the H100 and B200 chips that every AI lab needs to train models. More critically, they own **CUDA** — the software platform all AI researchers are trained on — creating switching costs so high customers can't leave. Net margins 55%, ROE 114%, revenue grew 85% YoY. Net cash $40B, near-zero debt.

## 2. TSM — Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

**Price: $423.93 | Panel: 2 bulls / 2 neutral / 1 bear | Signal: BUY ON DIP**

### The Business
TSMC builds chips for everyone else — Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm. ~90% of the world's most advanced chips (below 5nm) are made here. 3–5 year technology lead over rivals. Trades at the cheapest P/E (~22x) of all 7 stocks. One shadow: every single factory is on the island of Taiwan.

| Analyst | Signal | Conf | Key View |

### Why it's #2

**Entry:** $360–$380. At $424 it's fair but not cheap.

## 3. AVGO — Broadcom Inc.

**Price: $382.07 | Panel: 4 bulls / 1 neutral / 5 bears | Signal: HOLD — WAIT FOR PULLBACK**

### The Business
Broadcom has three powerful legs:
1. **Custom AI chips (XPUs)** — Google, Meta, and ByteDance pay Broadcom to design their own AI chips, bypassing NVIDIA's GPUs. Fastest-growing segment.
2. **Networking silicon** — Broadcom chips route data inside every major data center. No real competitor.
3. **VMware enterprise software** — acquired for $69B in 2023; generates massive recurring software revenue from enterprises globally.

Gross margins ~65%. CEO Hock Tan is considered one of the best capital allocators in tech. The $69B VMware deal loaded the balance sheet with $130B of goodwill and debt — the key risk.

### Fundamentals: Partial BULLISH (50/100)

**Price: $567.25 | Panel: 1 bull / 4 neutral / 6 bears | Signal: AVOID — MOST OVERVALUED**

| **#1 NVDA** | **Buy $175–$205** | Only bullish fundamentals score. CUDA moat. Broadest bull coalition. Already pulled back. |

| **#3 AVGO** | **Watch — Buy $290–$320** | 3 lollapalooza tailwinds. Damodaran FV $292 vs $382 today. 24% overvalued — smallest gap of the "avoid" group. |
| **#4 ASML** | **Watch — Buy $1,400–$1,500** | Best monopoly on earth. Just too expensive today. Wait for 25% pullback. |
| **#5 FN** | **Avoid — Buy $300–$360** | Great precision manufacturer, no IP. 52x PE needs 50% correction. |
| **#6 GEV** | **Avoid — Buy $600–$700** | Compelling power/AI story. EV/EBIT 178x, Damodaran FV $283 vs $940. 3.3x intrinsic. |
| **#7 AMAT** | **Avoid — Buy $345–$380** | Cyclical with declining earnings at 53x PE. Clearest overvaluation of all 7. |

### Single Pick: **NVDA**
Start a position at $205. Add at $175–$190. Full size at $160. 3–5 year horizon.

### If You Want Two Picks — Add **AVGO at $290–$320**
When AVGO corrects to Damodaran's $292 fair value, it becomes an exceptional buy. Three business lines (custom AI chips + networking monopoly + VMware software) make it the most diversified AI infrastructure play, with CEO Hock Tan's capital allocation track record as a bonus.

### What AVGO and GEV Add to the Picture
- **AVGO** reinforces that extraordinary businesses exist across the AI stack — but the valuation gap (24% overvalued) still needs to close before the risk/reward is compelling.
- **GEV** highlights the danger of narratively driven investing: "AI needs power → buy GEV" is a true statement, but it doesn't justify paying 178x EV/EBIT. At 3.3x Damodaran's intrinsic value, the stock is pricing in decades of perfect execution. Wait for $600–$700.
